title: BCC denies Gustafson comprehensive-plan amendment, 13.86 acres at 2005 S CR 16-A, Green Cove Springs (District 5) — Vice-Chairman Burke's motion
agendaItem: Item 20: Final Public Hearing on COMP 25-0010 (FLUM Agriculture→Rural Residential) and ZON 25-0007 (Rezoning Agriculture→Agricultural Residential)
motion: Vice-Chairman Kristen Burke moved to deny COMP 25-0010; seconded by Commissioner John Sgromolo
parcel: 16-06-26-015574-001-02 — 13.86+/- acres, 2005 S County Road 16 (CR 16-A), Green Cove Springs
location: The Springs planning district, District 5 (Commissioner Burke)
applicant: Sheryl Edlyn Gustafson (owner/homesteaded resident since 2013), represented at the hearing by Danielle Kitchens, real estate agent
staffRecommendation: Approval of both COMP 25-0010 and ZON 25-0007 — staff found the request consistent with the 2045 Comprehensive Plan, within the Urban Service Boundary, and consistent with surrounding land use
publicComment: Public hearing opened 5:54pm, closed 5:58pm by Chairman Betsy Condon; no speakers other than Ms. Kitchens are recorded. Extended Board discussion followed with staff and Ms. Kitchens covering development options under current AG zoning, surrounding properties, lot sizes, selling price, minimum-lot-size options, code requirements, water/sewer, density, and the applicant's residence, intent to sell, and future plans.
result: Motion to DENY carried 4-1 (Renninger dissenting, i.e. Renninger would have approved). Because the comprehensive-plan amendment was denied, the companion rezoning (ZON 25-0007) was not considered. Chairman Condon recommended the applicant reapply with a minimum lot size or as a PUD.
sourceNote: Confirmed against the official, e-signed BCC minutes (PrimeGov meetingTemplateId 8164, meeting id 1833) — see EV-010. Video available at www.claycountygov.com/government/clay-county-tv-and-video-archive, BCC Agenda, June 24, 2025, timestamp 1:56:56-2:20:20. This entry originally relied on a secondary AI-aggregated source (CitizenPortal.ai) whose commissioner-attribution was wrong (see EV-011 for the specific correction: no 'Commissioner John Burke' or 'Commissioner Magdalen' exists — the real mover was Kristen Burke herself). Recorded neutrally: a commissioner moving to deny an application against staff/CAC/Planning-Commission recommendations is a normal, lawful exercise of discretion and is not, by itself, evidence of any impropriety. The 'yes' votes for Compere and Sgromolo/Condon reflect the vote FOR denial (the motion on the floor); Renninger's 'no' reflects his vote against denial (i.e., for approval).
